meta.experiment: TS7 native-compiler code graph vs regex code graph

api.why_this_package: The published typescript@7.0.2 ships the same dist/api/* and dist/ast/* tree as @typescript/native-preview, and exports the same './unstable/sync' and './unstable/ast' subpaths. So the probe did not need the dev preview package: the stable tarball has the API, behind unstable/* exports.
entry_points: typescript/unstable/sync -> API, Snapshot, Project, Program, Checker, Symbol, NodeHandle, SymbolFlags
typescript/unstable/ast  -> SyntaxKind, is* type guards, node.forEachChild, createScanner
api.verdict: Usable today for a build-time code graph. It is one child-process round trip per checker query with no batch API, the whole surface is namespaced unstable/*, and several node kinds differ from what a JS dev expects (constructor, new). Fine as a batch extractor; not fine as a per-keystroke service.
worked: new API({collectTiming:true}) + updateSnapshot({openProjects:[tsconfig]}) loads a real tsconfig, honouring allowJs.
project.rootFiles gives the tsconfig include set (14 files); program.getSourceFileNames() also lists 193 lib/node_modules files.
program.getSourceFile(path) returns a full SourceFile with .text, .statements, getLineStarts(), getLineAndCharacterOfPosition().
node.forEachChild(cb) walks the tree; SyntaxKind + is.FunctionDeclaration/isCallExpression/... are exported.
checker.getSymbolAtLocation(node) resolves call targets, including cross-file; sym.valueDeclaration / sym.declarations give NodeHandles.
NodeHandle.resolve(project) turns a handle back into a node with .path and .getStart(), which is enough to map back to a chunk.
api.getTimingInfo().totals reports requestCount, roundTripMs, serverTimeMs, nodesMaterialized, bytesReceived.
friction: No batch checker API: 2,031 getSymbolAtLocation calls cost 2,245 IPC requests and ~220 ms of round trips. This dominates the build.
symbol.declarations are NodeHandles, not nodes; each one needs .resolve(project), another round trip.
symbol.flags & SymbolFlags.Alias is required before the target resolves across an import; getAliasedSymbol is a second round trip.
Class constructors are ConstructorDeclaration, not MethodDeclaration: isMethodDeclaration silently skips them (one chunk was missing until the regex diff caught it).
`new X()` is NewExpression, not CallExpression: a CALLS walker sees nothing unless it adds that kind explicitly.
CallExpression.getStart() is the start of the whole chain, so `a\n  .b()\n  .c()` reports the line of `a`. Site lines need the callee name token.
include globs are resolved relative to the tsconfig's own directory; a wrong ../ depth gives a silently empty project, not an error.
updateSnapshot({openProject}) is deprecated in favour of openProjects; the deprecated shim still works.
There is no forEachChild free function; traversal is a method on each node. Minor, but differs from the TypeScript 5/6 API.
The API spawns the native tsgo binary: ~50 ms per API instance, and api.close() must be called or the child stays alive.

timing.note: Process wall time includes ~65 ms of node startup for both extractors, so compare the in-process build times; process time is what a CLI pays.

precision_sample.method: Deterministic stride sampling over sorted edges (every n/20th). Verdicts were assigned by reading each source line.

meta.kind: same queries and qrels, same channel code, two graphs
meta.note: qrels are graph-derived (circular by construction). The only things that change between runs are the parser behind the graph and, in the ablation, the chunk text it produced.

ablation.name: ts7_boundaries_regex_text
ablation.purpose: isolate chunk-boundary fidelity from chunk-text truncation

meta.why: Each query set is generated from one graph's edges and then id-mapped onto both graphs, so the only asymmetry left is which graph the relations were read off.

meta.kind: capability test, graph-derived qrels (not human relevance)
meta.doc_unit: AST chunk (function/method/class/script body), full node text
meta.warning: The graph channel is evaluated against qrels built from the same CALLS edges it walks. It cannot lose by design on both@k; treat the deltas as an upper bound on channel value, not as evidence of quality.
